_comment: The agreed definition of 'good enough', enforced by evals/gate.py in CI.
Lowering a number here is a reviewable diff in the pull request that needs it -
that visibility is the point. Never relax a threshold in the same commit that
breaks it without saying why in the diff.
Set from the 2026-09-04 baseline, after the citation-fidelity repair. They sit
at or just below observed values rather than at a round 1.000, because
temperature=0 is not a determinism guarantee on a hosted MoE endpoint (see
docs/evals/baseline-2026-08-22.md's ZL-018 finding) and a gate that fires on
single-case run-to-run wobble teaches people to ignore it.
_rule_engine_coverage: Deterministic code, no model involved. Anything below 1.000 means the rule
engine and the golden labels have diverged, which is never acceptable and
_max_route_mismatches: Also deterministic: which route a case takes is decided by apply_rules.
Zero tolerance for the same reason.

_citation_fidelity: The project's one rule, tested mechanically. Observed 1.000 across two full
passes after the prompt v2 repair; the floor allows one case of the 27 to
wobble without failing CI, and no more.
_no_invented_numbers: Observed 1.000 after the scorer boundary fix for sub-area labels.
_states_both_values: Observed 1.000 in every pass of every baseline recorded so far. This is the
counterweight to citation_fidelity: a summary that cites perfectly but states
no values passes there and fails here.
_did_not_read_the_document: The PDF boundary in docs/rules.md, held rather than merely instructed.
1.000 in every pass ever recorded, and a keyword heuristic besides - a single
failure here is a real signal, so there is no wobble allowance.
_valid_structured_output: Strict JSON schema held. Transient Groq connection errors land here rather
than on a fidelity scorer, so this floor absorbs one failed call in 27; a
